parsed.summary: The Lean file proves two things. First, there is a finite connected bipartite 2-degenerate graph H on Fin q such that, under each of its 2-colourings, both colour classes contain a vertex of degree ≥ 3, and there are constants c, ε > 0 with c·n^{3/2+ε} ≤ ex(n,H) for all sufficiently large n. Second, Erdős's degeneracy conjecture fails: it is not true that every bipartite r-degenerate H (r > 0) has ex(n,H) = O(n^{2−1/r}). Both statements faithfully match Theorem 1.2 and its stated corollary. The main caveat is coverage: Theorem 1.1 (failure of compactness) is not formalized at all.

glossary.plain: N_G(v) ∩ s, the neighbours of v inside the finite set s
glossary.standard_concept: neighbourhood restricted to a vertex subset

glossary.plain: Every nonempty finite vertex set s contains a vertex with at most r neighbours in s, i.e. every nonempty induced subgraph has minimum degree ≤ r
glossary.note: The paper says 'subgraph' rather than 'induced subgraph'. The two are equivalent, since passing to a subgraph only lowers degrees.

glossary.plain: For all r > 0 and every bipartite r-degenerate graph H on Fin q, ex(n,H) = O(n^{2−1/r}) as n → ∞

lean_claims.plain: There exist q and a graph H on Fin q with these properties: H is connected, bipartite and 2-degenerate; for every proper 2-colouring of H and each colour, some vertex of that colour has degree > 2; and there exist reals c > 0, ε > 0 such that for all sufficiently large n, c·n^{3/2+ε} ≤ ex(n,H).
There exist r > 0 and a bipartite r-degenerate graph H on some Fin q such that ex(n,H) is not O(n^{2−1/r}).

paper_claims.plain: There is a finite nonempty family F of connected bipartite graphs, each containing a cycle, with ex(n,F) = O(n^{4/3−1/48}) and ex(n,F) = Ω(n^{4/3}) for each F ∈ F.
There exist a fixed connected bipartite 2-degenerate graph H and constants c, ε > 0 such that ex(n,H) ≥ c·n^{3/2+ε} for all sufficiently large n.
The conjecture that every bipartite r-degenerate H has ex(n,H) = O(n^{2−1/r}) is false, already for r = 2.

coverage.why: No statement about the compactness family appears in the file.
Same claim, plus an extra condition that both bipartition classes have maximum degree ≥ 3.
The negation of the conjecture exactly as stated in (3).

flags.explanation: The compactness counterexample, one of the paper's two main results, is not formalized.

The exponent is written `(3 : ℕ) / 2 + ε` with ε : ℝ. Lean's binop% elaborator should coerce the leaf (3 : ℕ) to ℝ, giving the real number 3/2. If ℕ division were used instead, the exponent would collapse to 1+ε, a much weaker claim.
flags.probe_idea: example (ε : ℝ) : ((3 : ℕ) / 2 + ε : ℝ) = (3/2 : ℝ) + ε := by norm_num

flags.explanation: There is an extra conjunct: for every 2-colouring, each colour class has maximum degree > 2. This rules out the known Füredi/AKS case and only strengthens the statement relative to the paper.
